channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: Street Fighter wins the weekend with $31 million and $51 million worldwide
item.description: Paramount's Street Fighter opened at No. 1 in North America and added $20.1 million from 65 overseas markets.

item.title: Apple staff are reported to warn iPhone Duo shoppers against walk-ins
item.description: With the $1,999 foldable sold out into late January, some Apple Store staff were told to discourage launch-day walk-ins.

item.title: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund
item.description: Anthropic plans to put 5% of its equity into a fund for charity and AI job impacts, with more added as its value rises.

item.title: Nathan Fielder's Holmes film opens to $15 million, a documentary near-record
item.description: A24's You Can See Everything took about $15 million from just 855 theaters, the second-best non-fiction opening ever.

item.title: Sam Altman confirms OpenAI is building a humanoid robot
item.description: OpenAI's chief said the company will build a humanoid robot and expects a demo in 2027, with 27 robotics jobs listed.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4's campaign hits 92% positive on Steam ahead of launch
item.description: About 2,900 of 3,156 Steam reviews recommend the early-access campaign, with DMZ opening October 20 and full launch October 23.

item.title: PlayStation 6 memory alone is claimed to cost over $680 per console
item.description: An insider says RAM and storage costs could push the next PlayStation past $1,000, as AI data centers drive memory prices up.

item.title: Chip stocks fall for an eighth straight day as AI spending doubts grow
item.description: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 3.83% on Friday, ending the week down 11.4%, led by memory makers.

item.title: Anthropic is reported to pitch its own AI safety bill to US lawmakers
item.description: Anthropic's draft would let authorities block a frontier model only for imminent risks above $1 billion or harm to over 50 people, reports say.

item.title: GTA VI's launch trailer gets picked apart a month before release
item.description: Rockstar's 90-second launch trailer is still being analysed, with Digital Foundry doubting it uses the PS5's new upscaler.

item.title: Anthropic says AI agents now log six times more work hours than its staff
item.description: An Anthropic report on its own workforce says agent work hours far outnumber employee hours and junior technical hiring has dropped sharply.

item.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 arrives on Netflix on October 20
item.description: The 10-episode standalone sequel to the 2022 anime is out Tuesday, with Cyberpunk 2077 on sale for 70% off on Steam.

item.title: Valve prices the Steam Frame headset from $1,059
item.description: Valve's Steam Frame costs $1,059 with 256GB or $1,299 with 1TB, with reservation holders able to order by December or in 2027.

item.title: Anthropic says Claude solved the mystery of where NIST's curve seeds came from
item.description: Claude traced the seeds behind widely used NIST elliptic curves to a simple random generator seeded with timestamps, Anthropic says.

item.title: Samsung is reported to use rival TSMC to make base dies for Nvidia's custom memory
item.description: Samsung will reportedly tap TSMC's 3nm process for the base die of Nvidia's custom HBM, its first such handoff.

item.title: Banks, airlines and retailers are locking AI agents out of their sites
item.description: Amazon, Delta and major US banks are blocking outside AI agents such as Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots from acting for users.

item.title: Antonio Banderas and Nicolas Cage join True Detective season 5
item.description: HBO confirmed the two stars for the next season, reportedly set in New York's Jamaica Bay, with filming in 2027.

item.title: Hack exposes data on about 7 million California public school students
item.description: A compromised login at testing provider Education Testing Service exposed names, addresses, demographics and disability status.

item.title: New Macs are reported for November 6 as a new iPad mini case leaks
item.description: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says new Macs arrive November 6, and a filing for an unreleased iPad mini case hints at a redesign.

item.title: Investors are reported to push back on Nscale's $35 billion IPO goal
item.description: Investors reportedly want the AI cloud firm valued at $16 billion to $19 billion, about half what it is seeking.

item.title: John Wilson is reported to be making a Harry Styles tour documentary
item.description: The How To with John Wilson creator is filming Styles' 30-night Madison Square Garden residency, with a cinema release under consideration.

item.title: Valve's invite-only Deadlock passes 300,000 players on Steam
item.description: Deadlock hit a peak of 303,347 concurrent players, making it Steam's fourth most-played game while still invite-only.

item.title: Apple launches HomeView, a $300 smart display, with a wider smart home lineup
item.description: Apple opened preorders for a 7-inch HomeView display, a new HomePod mini, Apple TV 4K and cameras, locks and thermostats.

item.title: US lends up to $4.4 billion to restart three nuclear plants for AI power
item.description: The Energy Department is backing restarts at Palisades, Crane and Duane Arnold, restoring about 2.25 gigawatts mainly for data centers.

item.title: Kid Rock releases a Christian album featuring Eminem
item.description: Halfway 2 Jesus includes Heal My Faith with Eminem, plus Lil Wayne and Jimmie Allen, despite the two rappers' opposite politics.

item.title: Konami's president says AI cannot replace the people behind great games
item.description: Hideki Hayakawa says generative AI will not change the games market much and that creators matter most.

item.title: Led Zeppelin licenses Stairway to Heaven to a film for the first time, for Narnia
item.description: Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew uses the song in its new trailer, after the band turned down films for decades.

item.title: Footage leaks from a reportedly cancelled Assassin's Creed set in ancient China
item.description: Clips of Assassin's Creed Destiny, said to be made by Tencent's TiMi Studio, surfaced from developer portfolios.

item.title: Tim Sweeney says AI can take over the routine work of coding
item.description: Epic's chief said about 70% of his time building Unreal Engine 1 went to routine typing and refactoring that AI can now handle.

item.title: Verizon will charge $10 a month to share one number across two iPhones
item.description: Verizon plans a monthly fee for iOS 27's feature that lets one number switch between a main and companion iPhone.

item.title: Korean publishers launch 'No Books, No AI' appeal over training on their books
item.description: Backed by 158 groups and 321 people, the appeal follows reports that Anthropic bought hundreds of thousands of Korean books for training.

item.title: Liquid Swords, the studio behind Samson, goes bankrupt
item.description: The Swedish studio founded by a former Just Cause director is bankrupt after months of unpaid wages, with about 30 jobs affected.

item.title: DeepSeek releases an open V4.1 Flash model with built-in web search
item.description: DeepSeek posted V4.1-Flash-1017 on Hugging Face under an MIT license, adding live search and page fetching.

item.title: Steam Next Fest opens today with a week of free demos
item.description: Valve's demo festival runs from October 19 to 26, with games such as Loftia and Stronghold 4 among those taking part.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, a huge open-weight model that runs on two Macs
item.description: Meta's 816-billion-parameter Muse Spark Open model is built for coding and agents and can run on two Mac Studio machines.

item.title: Whalefall opens fourth with $8 million
item.description: Disney's survival thriller took about $8 million from 3,065 theaters, short of expectations, with a B CinemaScore.

item.title: New Sense and Sensibility opens to $7.25 million with an A- CinemaScore
item.description: Focus Features' Jane Austen adaptation took an estimated $7.25 million from 2,545 theaters, with audiences rating it highly.

item.title: Chris Evans and Anya Taylor-Joy's Sacrifice climbs to No. 2 on Netflix
item.description: Netflix's hostage comedy, about a movie star taken captive by a cult at a charity gala, is its second most-watched US film.

item.title: Sega pulls the Total War: Shogun 2 remaster after an 'Overwhelmingly Negative' launch
item.description: Sega is temporarily removing the remaster from sale and restoring the original game after players reported bugs and possible AI-upscaled art.

item.title: Stolen ConnectWise credential used to sign in to 173 Microsoft 365 tenants
item.description: A compromised account for ConnectWise Cloud Backup was used to access Microsoft 365 tenants belonging to partners and customers.

item.title: Taiwan moves to make smuggling AI chips to China a crime
item.description: Taiwan plans to list AI servers and advanced chips as controlled goods, making unauthorized shipments to Chinese buyers a criminal offence.

item.title: Apple's new App Store rules target AI deepfakes and 'nudify' apps
item.description: Developers must now prevent and remove AI-made nonconsensual intimate images, and apps that hide such features from reviewers are banned.
